newsitem.title: USA: Fran approaches coast of Carolinas.
newsitem.headline: Fran approaches coast of Carolinas.

text.p: The National Hurricane Center warned that tropical storm force winds would reach North and South Carolina Thursday afternoon as Hurricane Fran approached, packing sustained winds near 115 mph (185 mph).

At 11 a.m. EDT (1500 GMT), Hurricane Fran's center was near latitude 31.5 north and longitude 77.4 west, or about 180 miles (290 km) south-southeast of the border of South Carolina and North Carolina, the National Hurricane Center said.
The storm was moving north-northwest near 16 mph (26 kmh), motion expected to continue through Thursday night.

"On this track, the center of the hurricane is expected to be near the coast within the warning area tonight," the hurricane center said. Forecasters said little change in strength was expected before landfall and that hurricane force winds were expected to spread inland as far as 100 miles (161 km) from the coast in Fran's path.
At 11:00 a.m. EDT (1500 GMT), hurricane warnings were in effect from Edisto Beach, South Carolina, to North Carolina's border with Virginia, including Pamlico and Albemarle Sounds.

A hurricane watch and a tropical storm warning were in effect form north of the North Carolina/Virginia border to Chincoteague, Virginia, including the Greater Hampton Roads area. A tropical storm warning was in effect for the lower Chesapeake Bay.
A hurricane warning from north of Brunswick, Georgia, to just south of Edisto Beach was changed to a tropical storm warning.
Forecasters also warned of tides 12 to 16 feet above normal (4 to 5.3 metres) possible near and to the northeast of where the center makes landfall over the Carolinas.
Rainfall totals of 5 to 10 inches (12.5 to 25 cm) were expected along Fran's path, with the rainfall threat increasing over higher terrain during the next 24 hours.
Isolated tornadoes also were possible over portions of the two states.
Forecasters also were watching the eighth tropical depression of the Atlantic hurricane season, which was moving westward toward the Leeward Islands of the Caribbean at 13 mph (20 kmh).

At 11:00 a.m. EDT (1500 GMT), the depression was near latitude 14.5 north and longitude 52.1 west, or about 610 miles (980 km) east of the less Antilles, with maximum sustained winds near 35 mph (55 kmh).
